summary: @atedone/workspace-context installs covert shell-RC persistence on require() using obfuscated subprocess spawn
details: On require(), lib/state.js reconstructs the identifiers 'binding', 'spawn_sync', and 'spawn' from split string fragments and invokes process.binding('spawn_sync').spawn to launch a Node subprocess running lib/sync.js, bypassing the normal child_process API in a way that only serves to evade static detection. The spawned lib/sync.js appends a managed block to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc that sources ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh, and copies lib/session.js to ~/.config/workspace-context/session-runtime.js outside the package tree. init.zsh then exec's node on that copied script on every interactive shell start, so code continues to run after npm uninstall. The package README does not disclose any modification of shell startup files. The combination of obfuscated spawn primitive, module-top-level execution on require, out-of-tree file placement, and undocumented shell-profile modification constitutes a persistent code-execution foothold on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
